corrections.claimed_speedup: Current README matrix (35 scenarios, Linux x86_64, measured 2026-09-30, revision 8fa2a48 = v0.12.11; QuickJS = the same binary with the JIT detached, QuickJS-NG fd0a0210): versus QuickJS 23 scenarios faster, 7 tied, 5 slower; e.g. scalar-control-flow 49.2x faster (2.13 ms vs 0.0434 ms per ten calls), scalar-expressions 47.4x, fibonacci-iterative 45.8x, quickjs-bitops 42.6x, fibonacci-recursive 27.1x (9.91 ms vs 0.361 ms), float64-dense 22.2x; slower cases collections 0.98x, strings-json 0.96x, json-codec 0.96x, map-set-bigint 0.99x, exceptions-promises-async 0.98x. Versus Bun 1.4.0 all 35 scenarios are slower (closest fibonacci-recursive 0.73x of Bun speed, widest methods-dynamic 0.012x).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: rustc 1.98.1 / LLVM 22.1.8, release build (harness built with 'cargo build --release --manifest-path benchmarks/Cargo.toml --bins'); JIT back end is Cranelift 0.116 (jit/Cargo.toml); QuickJS-NG commit fd0a0210b7be00957751871e7e01b8291268fc29 compiled through the sys crate's build.rs with the cc crate's release defaults (C compiler and version not named); Bun 1.4.0 default flags, launched from a .mjs file
corrections.stars_or_usage: 15 stars, 1 fork (GitHub fork of DelSkayn/rquickjs); published on crates.io as quickjs-jit (latest 0.12.6, 2026-09-03, 110 downloads); the measured 0.12.11 exists only in git
corrections.caveats: First-party matrix run on the author's own machine, though the harness, scripts, raw process records, metadata and binary hashes are all in the repo. Not a V8 win: every scenario is slower than Bun (JavaScriptCore) and V8 was not measured. The interpreter control is QuickJS-NG (fd0a0210) in the same binary with the JIT detached, not Bellard's QuickJS. Wins are on scalar and numeric kernels (many 20-50x); string, JSON, collection, regexp and exception scenarios are tied or 1-4% slower. v0.12.11 fixed a 0.12.10 regression in real gpui-shell renders by deferring P2 opcodes, which gave back exceptions-sync (0.21x the speed of 0.12.10) and for-of-array (0.36x) to interpreter speed. The protocol warms 640 calls and polls the JIT after every batch, so embedders that never poll see different tier-up behaviour; the diagnostics table shows compilation still active during timing on some kernels (float64-dense: only 4 of 30 processes quiet, 29 outlier batches; numeric 9 quiet). The JIT is Rust (Cranelift 0.116) over a vendored C engine, outside a strict C++ filter. Development is AI-assisted (AGENTS.md; recent commits co-authored by claude). crates.io has only 0.12.6; the README warns that runtime and core crates must share an exact patch version.

notes: All quoted numbers match the README's current matrix row by row; metadata checked on the GitHub page (MIT, 15 stars, not archived, last commit 2026-09-30) and crates.io. The repo is a GitHub fork of DelSkayn/rquickjs, but the JIT is new work, so it is not a duplicate of the listed QuickJS or QuickJS-NG entries. It is a JIT, so the 'jits' category may fit better than language-interpreters.

corrections.caveats: Numbers come from the README of the Pyccel developers' benchmark repository (pyccel/pyccel-benchmarks, 5 stars), not from Numba's repo; the Numba README gives no numbers. The dev-branch run (dated Mon Aug 3 10:56:24 UTC 2026) is a GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest job on a shared VM with no CPU model recorded, timed with python3 -m timeit best-of-5 rather than pyperf. The CPython column runs scalar loops that index NumPy arrays element by element, the slowest way to use NumPy, so the ratios (1.4x to 451.5x, geometric mean about 115x, derived from page data) do not transfer to code that is already vectorised. Numba is compiled with fastmath=True. It is the weakest accelerator on FD Laplace (1.4x over CPython) and trails pythran_gnu by 4.6x to 8.4x on the four finite-difference kernels (derived from page data), while beating pythran_gnu on RK4 (127 ms vs 152 ms). Measured version 0.66.0; PyPI is at 0.68.0. Compile time (unit is CPU seconds) is 0.33 to 6.75 s per kernel for Numba.

notes: All CPython and numba values in claimed_speedup match the dev-branch table and the derived ratios check out (geometric mean 114.9x). The requirements file the search agent could not open is version_specific_results/devel_performance_312_requirements.txt; it pins numba 0.66.0 and the workflow pins Python 3.12. Numba is a JIT, so the 'jits' category may fit better than language-interpreters.
